venue.name: Qualicum Beach Historical and Museum Society
venue.description: The Qualicum Beach Museum is the community museum for Qualicum Beach and the surrounding area, run by the Qualicum Beach Historical and Museum Society, which was incorporated in 1984. It holds one of the largest paleontology collections in Western Canada alongside exhibits on Qualicum First Nation history, local social history upstairs, an oral history room and a Powerhouse building about power and energy. Outside there is a small garden with a totem pole carved by Simon Charlie, a gazebo, a carved statue and a heritage cabin. Admission is by donation, with $5 suggested for adults and $2 for children, and school tours are available on request.
venue.address: 587 Beach Road, Qualicum Beach, B.C. V9K 1K7
venue.hours_notes: Summer, June through September, Tuesday to Saturday 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Winter, October through May, Tuesday and Thursday 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. and Saturday 1 p.m. to 4 p.m.
venue.seasonal_notes: Two temporary exhibits are running. The Island in the Middle of Everywhere, a photographic exhibition about Xwe'etay and Lasqueti Island, is on display until October 8, 2026. We Have The Power, in the Powerhouse building, is on until January 2027. The museum also runs a Children's Museum Day every August, which includes a shake splitting activity at the Pioneer House on the grounds.
venue.price_year_or_season: No year is printed against the suggested donation or the $25 membership fee. The temporary exhibits carry end dates of October 8, 2026 and January 2027, so both were still running when we checked.

programs.name: School tour
programs.description: The museum takes school groups on a tour of its fossil collection and its local history exhibits, on request. It says students learn about the social and natural history of Qualicum Beach and area through hands-on activities and inquiry-based learning. The museum is working with district schools to re-develop its educational programs around the K-12 BC curriculum, and says school tours are still available in the meantime. Nothing is published about how long a tour runs, how many children it takes, what ages it suits, how much notice is needed, or whether a group pays anything beyond the museum's usual donation.
programs.what_children_do: Look at fossils and objects from the town's past on the ground floor, then go up the stairs into the rooms about fishing, logging, the old train station and the Qualicum Beach Hotel. The museum says students take part in hands-on activities rather than only looking.
programs.our_note: Their school programs are being rewritten, so what you get is whatever staff can put together for you rather than a set lesson. Ask what the tour covers and how long it runs before you commit a morning to it. The social history rooms are up a flight of stairs, which is worth knowing if you are bringing a pushchair or a child who cannot manage them.
programs.practical_summary: Nothing is published about toilets, a place to eat indoors, step free access or where a bus can park, so those are all worth a phone call. Admission is by donation and the grounds outside, with a garden, a gazebo and a totem pole, are open to walk around.
programs.extra_fees_note: Admission to the museum is by donation. The suggested donation is $5 for adults and $2 for children. Nothing says whether a school or daycare group is asked for anything different.
programs.evidence: School tours are still available upon request. For more information or to book a tour, please contact the Museum.

images.alt: A red brick building with a steep gabled roof and a timber porch over its front door, a hanging sign reading Qualicum Beach Museum on the wall beside it, and a gravel path leading in from the road past a large white sign on a black fence.

A wide gravel courtyard with a carved wooden totem pole on a round concrete base at its centre, planted beds with red-leaved maples around it, a timber gazebo with benches on the left and a red brick building on the right.

gaps: NO PRICE FOR A GROUP. Admission is by donation, with $5 for adults and $2 for children suggested. That is neither free nor a price, so no cost has been recorded. Nothing says whether a school or daycare group is asked for a set fee, a per-child donation or nothing at all. This is the first thing to settle on the phone.

youngest age welcomed is not stated anywhere, and no age or grade range is published for the school tour. The only grade reference on the site is that they are re-developing programs to suit the K-12 BC curriculum, which describes the curriculum, not who the tour is for, so it has not been turned into a range.

no capacity is published for a school tour, and no minimum group size. The only capacity figure anywhere on the site is for the QB Reads writers series, which says a space in the museum buildings or grounds can host up to 30 people. That is a different offering and has not been used as the tour capacity.
no lead time is published. The tour is described as available upon request with no notice period stated.
no duration is published for the school tour.
washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site.
no indoor lunch space is mentioned. There is a gazebo on the grounds and a garden, but nothing says a group may eat there.
no rain backup is stated. The museum itself is indoors, but nothing covers what happens to a group booked for the outside exhibits in bad weather.
step free access and stroller access are not addressed. The site says the social history exhibits are reached by going upstairs, and nothing says whether there is a lift or an alternative route.
bus parking is not mentioned. The site says only that the museum sits across from the E&N Railway station on Beach Road.

months and days for the school tour are unknown, not year round. The museum's own opening days change with the season, but nothing says which of those days tours are run on, so the days have been left blank rather than copied from the opening hours.

TWO EMAIL ADDRESSES. The site gives both qbmuseumadmin@shaw.ca and qbmuseum2@shaw.ca under Email Us, on the home page and again on the contact page, without saying which is for bookings. The first has been recorded. Neither is hidden behind Cloudflare email protection, both were read directly from the live page.

no booking route is named for a school tour. The site says only to contact the museum, and offers a phone number, two email addresses, a contact form with a CAPTCHA and social media messaging. Email has been recorded as the route because an address is published, but the site does not say so itself.

THE MAP EMBED IS A VIEWPORT CENTRE, NOT A PIN. The Google Maps embed on their contact page carries only a map centre, at -124.4476878 and 49.350242, with a place reference but no place pin coordinates. The coordinates in this record were geocoded from the published street address instead, and land on the museum building.
The postal code on the site is V9K 1K7. The address record returned by geocoding gives V9K 2H7 for the same building. The site's own version has been kept.

The footer copyright line reads 2024 while news items on the same page are dated 2026, so the footer is stale. Everything else on the page, including the hours and the admission line, was read from the live page on 2026-09-10.

CHILDREN'S MUSEUM DAY is described as taking place in August every year, with a shake splitting activity at the Pioneer House on the grounds. No date, time, age range, cost or booking route is published for it, and it is a public day rather than a group booking, so it has not been recorded as a program. Worth asking about next spring.
The site has no plan your visit or accessibility page at all, which is why so many of the practical fields here are blank.
